name: skills
readmeExcerpt:
## Android skills

**Android skills** are a dedicated repository of **AI-optimized, modular instructions** and
resources, to help agents better understand and execute specific patterns that follow the best
practices and guidance on Android development
from [developer.android.com](https://developer.android.com).

Android skills follow the [open-standard agent skills](https://agentskills.io/home) - markdown
files (SKILL.md) that provide a technical specification of a task, and **ground LLMs** with
information on specialized domains and workflows.

Our Android skill development focuses on **use cases and workflows where evaluations show LLMs
underperform**.
We aren't prioritizing well-established areas where LLMs are already proficient, such
as basic Jetpack Compose best practices.

To learn more, read the official documentation:

- [Android skills](https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-skills)
- [Android CLI](https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-cli)
- [Android Studio](https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/skills)

### Install Android skills

Use Android CLI to install a specific skill into the current directory:

```
android skills add r8-analyzer --project=.
```

Use Android CLI to install all Android skills to directories for all detected agents:

```
android skills add --all
```

If you don't have any existing agent directories and don't specify particular agents, the skills
will be installed for Gemini and Antigravity at `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills`.

**Options:**

- `--all` - Add all Android skills. If omitted, only the `android-cli` skill will be installed.
- `--agent` - A comma-separated list of agents to install the skill for. If omitted, the skill will be installed for all detected agents.
- `--project` - Path to a project root in which to install the skills.


To update all skills or specific ones, run:

```
android skills update --all
android skills update wear-compose-m3
```

### Install as an agent plugin

**Claude Code**:

```
/plugin marketplace add android/skills
/plugin install android-skills@android-skills
```

**Codex:**

```
codex plugin marketplace add android/skills
codex plugin add android-skills@android-skills
```

### Activate skills

Your agent automatically activates skills that are relevant to your task. To use a skill, prompt your agent to complete a task that is related to the skill, for example "Make my app UI edge-to-edge." The agent should automatically find and use the skill if it has been installed.

## Disclaimer

AI can make mistakes, so always double-check the results.

## Contributing

Submit a GitHub issue to provide feedback, report issues, or make new skill requests and changes.

Public contributions are not accepted at this time.

## License

Android Skills is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE.txt). See the `LICENSE.txt` file
for
details.

## Review our community guidelines

This project follows
[Google's Open Source Community Guidelines](https://opensource.google/conduct/).

aiSummary.oneLiner: Instructions (SKILL.md) to help AI coding agents write modern Android code and avoid outdated patterns.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: The Android Skills repository provides a specific set of instructions formatted as a SKILL.md file for AI coding agents. It guides large language models to generate modern, idiomatic Android code using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. The project addresses the problem of AI agents hallucinating outdated Java patterns or legacy XML layouts common in their training data. By providing explicit context and rules, it ensures AI-generated code aligns with current Google-endorsed architectural standards like MVVM. This drastically improves the usefulness of AI coding assistants for modern Android development.
keyFeatures: AI agent instructions: Formats development guidelines specifically for consumption by large language models.
Modern toolkit enforcement: Directs agents to prioritize Kotlin and Jetpack Compose over legacy alternatives.
Pattern correction: Explicitly instructs AI tools to avoid hallucinating outdated architectural patterns.
Standardized context: Provides a drop-in file to unify the coding style generated by various AI assistants.
Google standards alignment: Ensures output matches the latest recommended practices for Android development.

useCases.title: Guiding AI code generation
useCases.description: Provide clear instructions to AI assistants like Copilot to ensure they write modern Android code.

useCases.title: Preventing legacy hallucinations
useCases.description: Stop language models from generating outdated Java or XML layout code in new projects.

useCases.title: Standardizing AI output
useCases.description: Ensure multiple developers using AI tools produce consistent, idiomatic Kotlin codebases.

useCases.title: Learning prompt engineering
useCases.description: Analyze the repository to understand how to write effective system instructions for coding agents.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Android developers utilizing AI coding assistants who want to ensure generated code is modern and idiomatic. Teams looking to standardize the output of language models across their projects.
